# simttepower

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

simttepower is a companion to [simtte](https://github.com/csetraynor/simtte)
(>= 1.1.0), providing trial replication and simulation-based power and
operating-characteristic analysis on top of simtte's single-cohort PK/PD
time-to-event simulator. Given a trial design and a grid of scenarios that
vary any one factor (a model parameter, a formula coefficient, a dosing
regimen, a sampling schedule, sample size, follow-up, or covariate
distribution), simttepower replicates each scenario, applies one or more
analysis functions to each simulated trial, and summarises operating
characteristics -- power and type I error -- across the grid. A run can
execute sequentially, across local worker processes, or split into
independent chunks for a job scheduler; all three give byte-identical
results for the same seed.

## Installation

simtte isn't on CRAN yet, so install it first, then simttepower from
[GitHub](https://github.com/):

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("csetraynor/simtte")
pak::pak("csetraynor/simttepower")
```

## Example

Two arms of a built-in PK/PD hazard model, varying sample size on the
experimental arm, replicated, summarised, and plotted:

```{r example}
library(simttepower)

comparator <- arm(label = "comparator", n = 30, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 1, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15))
experimental <- arm(label = "experimental", n = 30, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 3, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15))

design <- trial_design(
  arms = list(comparator, experimental),
  analyses = list(coxph = analysis_coxph)
)

grid <- scenario_grid(design, over = list(arm = "experimental",
  field = "n", values = c(30, 60, 90)))

res <- power_sim(grid, n_sims = 8, seed = 1, progress = FALSE)
summary(res)
```

```{r example-plot}
plot_power(summary(res), x = "n")
```

`power_sim(..., workers = 2)` dispatches across local worker processes
instead of running sequentially; `power_sim_chunks()`/`power_sim_chunk()`/
`power_sim_merge()` split a run into independent chunks for a job
scheduler (SGE/Slurm templates ship in `inst/templates/`). Both give
byte-identical results to the sequential run above -- see
`vignette("power-analysis")` for the full walkthrough, a real
dosing-regimen contrast, a covariate-adjusted analysis, and a
direction-aware rejection rule.

**Development note**: the `Remotes: csetraynor/simtte` entry in
`DESCRIPTION` (for installing simtte from GitHub pre-CRAN) is removed
before any CRAN submission.
